subject:
Demo recap + proposed POC plan

FinServeCo
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - FinServeCo

Hi Oliver / Sonia,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning - really appreciated the team walking us through the card-authorization flow and the latency constraints you’re seeing at peak. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan so we can get alignment on success criteria and next steps.

Demo highlights:
- Walked through Redwood inference runtime handling of streaming responses and prefix caching for repeated authorization prompts.
- Showed cost/latency trade-offs across 8-bit quantized model and a 16-bit baseline.
- Reviewed observability: per-route token cost breakdowns and per-request traces in the Console.

Proposed POC objective:
- Validate that Redwood can meet 100ms median generation latency for inline authorization prompts at 95th percentile traffic for a single region, while reducing token cost by at least 30% vs your current endpoint.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: median generation <= 100ms and p95 <= 220ms under a representative traffic profile (we can use your sample trace).
2) Cost: per-invocation token cost reduction >= 30% after batching and KV caching enabled.
3) Quality: end-to-end accuracy on a 200-case prompt set with <= 5% regression vs current model outputs.
4) Operational: end-to-end integration with your auth service and no changes required to your frontend calls (same request/response shape).

POC plan (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): exchange sample traces, prompt set, and dataset for quality checks.
- Week 1: Redwood spins up a dedicated evaluation endpoint in our staging cluster; ingests sample trace and runs baseline.
- Week 2: Tuning: batching/caching profiles and quantization tests; run load tests to hit p95 target.
- Week 3: Joint validation with FinServe engineering on 200-case prompt set and finalize integration guidance.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Aisha (technical lead), Marissa (customer success/POC coordinator), Dylan (infra & perf).
- FinServe: Oliver (eng lead), Sonia (product).

Attachments: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (POC timeline + test plan), redwood-sla-summary.xlsx (SLA/metrics we’ll track).

Next steps:
1) Oliver - can you send the sample trace and the 200-case prompt set by EOD Tuesday?
2) We’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff on Wednesday to align infra and access.

Thanks - excited to move forward.

Best,
Aisha
--
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finserve.co>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@finserve.co>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - FinServeCo

Thanks Aisha - really clear. Quick questions from our side before we kick off: 

1) For the latency target, is the 100ms median for token generation only, or end-to-end (including network + your edge routing)? We need to know since our front end adds ~15-25ms.
2) For the cost reduction, can you share a ballpark on how batching & caching typically performs for small prompts (20-60 tokens)?
3) On security: will the POC run within our VPC or on Redwood-hosted infra? We need to confirm SOC2 controls and data handling.

We should be able to get you the trace and the prompt set by Tuesday EOD. Also Sonia asked if we can extend the POC timeline by a week if we uncover integration dependencies.

Oliver

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan - FinServeCo

Thanks Oliver - good clarifying questions. I’ll answer inline and propose minor adjustments: 

1) Latency scope: the POC success criteria will be measured end-to-end from FinServe’s service to the Redwood endpoint and back (so includes network). Given your front end overhead, we’ll target Redwood generation median <= 85ms so combined you’re within the 100-110ms envelope. We’ll document the measurement points in the kickoff.

2) Cost for small prompts: batching & KV caching still provide meaningful savings for short prompts because of prefix reuse across repeated auth prompts. For 20-60 token prompts we typically see a 20-40% reduction depending on cache hit rate; our PoC tests will model your real reuse patterns.

3) Security/hosting: for the initial evaluation we can run in Redwood-hosted staging with encrypted links and access controls. If you need VPC/private deployment during the POC, we can evaluate Dedicated or Private options but that adds ~1 week to setup. Given Sonia’s note, we can extend the timeline by a week and plan a backup to move to a VPC-hosted endpoint if needed.

Proposed small timeline update: shift joint validation to Week 4 (instead of Week 3) to allow for infra adjustments if you opt for a VPC test. \

I’ve attached an updated POC outline and a short SLA metrics sheet.

Can we lock a 30-minute kickoff Wed 4/21 at 10:00am PT? If that doesn’t work, propose alternatives.

Thanks - Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
